clue.text: Last month Irish town almost finished in sporting event

parts.note: December is the last month of the year, abbreviated DEC

indicators.note: almost means the town's name stops one letter short of the end

parts.note: Athlone is a town in the Irish midlands

explanation.surface: Late last month a race in an Irish town nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the final E from ATHLONE, leaving ATHLON; 'finished in' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-discipline athletics contest is a classic example of a sporting event.

clue.text: Ideal partner met aboard, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone may have met the perfect partner on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome, desirable lover is the ideal partner of daydreams.

clue.text: Chap in charge beginning to reprimand soldier, part of palace guard?

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer, the man in charge

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An officer starts to scold a soldier on royal guard duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the palace 'guard' is a royal pet dog, not a sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen famously kept small Welsh dogs that guarded Buckingham Palace in a playful sense.

clue.text: Artist accepting a husband from Pacific island

indicators.note: accepting means the painter's name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A painter takes in a married man from a South Sea island.
explanation.walkthrough: Gauguin painted in Tahiti, but the artist here is TITIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or thing of Tahiti is described as coming from that Pacific island.

clue.text: No fellow for mixing?

indicators.note: mixing means the letters are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who doesn't socialise is asked about himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person who prefers working alone avoids company.

clue.text: Protection for someone eating game with people

parts.note: nap is a card game
kin means one's people, family

explanation.surface: A diner is shielded during a game with company.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth laid on the lap shields a diner's clothes from spills at the table.

clue.text: Late time to say one's piece

indicators.note: to say means the word for the chess piece is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a knight is one of a chess player's pieces

explanation.surface: A speaker waits until late to deliver a prepared speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' suggests a speech or recital, but it is a chessman; the silent K vanishes when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours after dark are the late part of the day.

clue.text: Piece moved up to take minor piece

indicators.note: moved up means the word reads upwards in this down clue

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun
to get is to take

explanation.surface: In chess, a piece advances to capture a minor piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface is false: 'Piece' is a gun, which 'moved up' turns to NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lump, like gold found by a prospector, is a minor piece.

clue.text: Cricket team's attractive member

definitions.note: the definition carries 's for 'is', linking it to the wordplay

parts.note: glam is short for glamorous, attractive
a member is a limb or body part, an organ

explanation.surface: A good-looking player belongs to a cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the Welsh county cricket club is GLAM plus ORGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh county club is one of England and Wales's first-class cricket sides.

clue.text: Tax — it's featured in article

indicators.note: featured in means the word goes inside the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
it's is read as 'it is', giving the word it

explanation.surface: A tax is the subject of a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper story but is the grammatical article THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a levy of one tenth of produce paid to the church.

clue.text: Some bear the name of Clay

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people carry the surname of the boxer Cassius Clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottery made of baked clay is described as earthenware, so the adjective means made of clay.

clue.text: Part of book — a religious work showing historical scenes

parts.note: a page is one leaf or side of a book
NT is the New Testament, a religious work

explanation.surface: An illustrated page from a sacred text depicts scenes from history.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the descriptive phrase 'showing historical scenes', standing for the spectacle that does so.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a public spectacle of costumed tableaux showing episodes from history.

clue.text: I'll come in extremely wet

indicators.note: come in means the letter goes inside the word for extremely

parts.note: most means extremely, as in 'most kind'
I'll is read as 'I will', so the letter I is what will come in

explanation.surface: Someone warns that they will arrive soaking wet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'll come in' as 'I will come in': the I goes inside MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp or slightly wet things are moist.

clue.text: Royal emblem otherwise represented

indicators.note: represented is read as re-presented, its letters set out again in another order

explanation.surface: A royal badge is depicted in some different manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' is read as re-presented, the letters of 'otherwise' set out anew.
explanation.definitionFit: The white rose was the badge of the royal House of York.

clue.text: In general, succeeded in top gear

parts.note: overall means in general, taken as a whole
s. is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A driver, on the whole, succeeds by staying in top gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top gear' looks like a car's highest gear, but it is clothing worn over the top of other clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are a protective garment worn on top of ordinary clothes.

clue.text: Get ride of date — behave tyrannically, heartlessly

parts.note: an era is a date or period in history

indicators.note: heartlessly means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to dictate is to give orders like a tyrant

explanation.surface: A tyrant wants to be rid of a date and acts cruelly.
explanation.walkthrough: The paper prints 'ride' for 'rid' in the definition. 'heartlessly' removes the middle T of DICTATE to give DICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something completely is to remove it, root and branch.

clue.text: A ruler provided a site for mausoleum out East

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A ruler chose a place in the East for his tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: GR stands for George Rex, the royal cipher of King George.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taj Mahal, the great Indian mausoleum, stands in Agra.

clue.text: Article. Lancelot smashed without warning

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: smashed means the name is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A knight of the Round Table is suddenly crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of LANCELOT gives LLATONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens suddenly happens abruptly, without any warning.

clue.text: Manage to get away with kidnap

definitions.meaning: to succeed in pulling something off without trouble
to abduct someone, seizing and taking them away

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to pull off a feat and to abduct someone.

clue.text: Richard Murphy, it's said, is a despot

indicators.note: it's said means the pieces are spoken to give a word that sounds alike

parts.note: Dick is short for Richard, and murphy is slang for a potato, a tater

explanation.surface: A man named Richard Murphy is reported to be a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'murphy' is old slang for a potato, from its Irish associations; 'tater' is a colloquial potato.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler wielding unchecked power is a tyrant or autocrat.

clue.text: Career that leads to extremely advantageous retirement

indicators.note: leads means the leading, first, letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A career path ends in a very comfortable retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' as a noun suggests a profession; here it is the verb to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush wildly along, as is to tear along.

clue.text: Not insane, not a liar, not normal

indicators.note: not normal means the letters are put in an abnormal order

explanation.surface: A witness insists they are sane and honest but admits to being odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A sane person thinks logically and soundly, so is sensible in mind.

clue.text: Local worker has to stop carrying weapon

indicators.note: carrying means the word for stop holds the weapon inside

parts.note: to ban is to stop or prohibit
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood employee has to stop bearing arms.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub, so its worker serves drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pulls pints at the pub works behind the bar.

clue.text: Blind summit — stop sign should be put up!

parts.note: ben is a Scottish mountain peak

indicators.note: put up means the word reads upwards in this down clue

parts.note: a red light is the sign to stop

explanation.surface: Approaching a blind summit, drivers are told to erect a stop sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blind' is not sightless but a drinking spree; BEN is Scottish for mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a blind or bender is a heavy drinking binge.

clue.text: Warship, having left from River Plate, at sea

indicators.note: at sea means the remaining letters are in confusion, rearranged

explanation.surface: A warship has departed from the River Plate and is now on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left from' tells you to remove L from RIVER PLATE before 'at sea' rearranges the rest; the River Plate is South America's great estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: A privately owned armed vessel licensed to attack enemy shipping served as a warship.

clue.text: Suddenly drop round

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to flop down heavily and to be pleasantly fat.

clue.text: Understood address accommodates one

indicators.note: accommodates means the word for address holds the numeral inside

parts.note: address can mean skill and adroitness, as does tact
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone understood that an address has room for one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' suggests a home; here it is dexterity in handling people.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is implied and understood without being spoken.

clue.text: Pass with acceptable mark in writing

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A student passes with an acceptable grade in written work.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation sign of two dots is a mark used in written text.

clue.text: Venus de Milo is, in one piece, according to 'Arry

indicators.note: a Cockney like 'Arry drops his aitches, so the H is lost

parts.note: in one piece means safe and undamaged

explanation.surface: A Cockney remarks that the famous statue is intact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arry, Harry with no H, stands for a Cockney speaker who drops H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Greek statue has lost both its arms, so it is literally armless.

clue.text: Bunting -— there's plenty around in port

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the port's name

parts.note: Oran is a port in Algeria

indicators.note: around means the word for plenty is turned round

parts.note: a lot means plenty

explanation.surface: A display of flags and pennants decorates a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' looks like festive flags but is the songbird; 'around' reverses the word for plenty, and Oran is an Algerian port.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European songbird of the bunting family.

clue.text: Pound note tucked inside dress carefully

indicators.note: tucked inside means the note goes within the word for pound

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, as is a pen
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A banknote is slipped into a dress with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound note' reads as a banknote, but the two words work separately: an enclosure and a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp, groom and smarten oneself fussily is to preen.

clue.text: Character given priority when penniless

indicators.note: penniless means without a penny, abbreviated P, so that letter goes

parts.note: preference means priority, as in being given preference

explanation.surface: Someone of good character is given priority once they are broke.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a written testimonial from a former employer, also called a reference.
